LAWS OF MALAYSIA

WEEKLY HOLIDAYS ACT 1950

[ACT 220]

WEEKLY HOLIDAYS RULES 1951

(Made under section 14)

(Revised—2023)

[20 September 1951; L.N. 577/1951]

Citation

1. These rules may be cited as the Weekly Holidays Rules 1951.

Notice under subsections 3(2), 5(4) and 7(2) of the Act

2. (1) The notice referred to in subsections 3(2), 5(4) and 7(2) of the Act shall be

in Form A as specified in the Schedule.

(2) The proprietor or manager of any shop affected by subsections 3(1), 5(1)

and 7(1) of the Act shall send a true copy of every such notice and, where any alteration

in such notice becomes necessary, a true amended copy of such notice to the nearest

Labour Office—

(a) in the case of a shop affected by subsections 3(1) and 7(1)

of the Act, within two weeks of the commencement of any trade or

business in such shop; and

(b) in the case of a shop affected by subsection 5(1) of the Act,

within thirty days of the date of publication of a notification in the

Gazette under subsection 5(1) of the Act or within two weeks

of the commencement of any trade or business in such shop,

whichever is the later.

(3) Any alteration to a notice in Form A other than as referred to

in subrules 4(1) and (2), shall be notified in writing to the nearest Labour Office

not later than two weeks before such alteration becomes effective.

Notice under subsection 3(4) of the Act

3. (1) The notice referred to in subsection 3(4) of the Act shall be in Form B

as specified in the Schedule.

(2) The proprietor of any unassisted shop shall send a true copy of every notice

referred to in subrule (1) or, where any alteration in such notice becomes necessary,

a true amended copy of the notice, to the nearest Labour Office within the State

in which the shop is situated, within two weeks of the commencement of any trade or

business in such shop.

Application for substitution and alteration of holiday

4. (1) An application for the substitution of some other day in any particular

week for Friday or Sunday under the proviso (b) to subsection 3(1) of the Act

may be made—

(a) in person at the nearest Labour Office not later than noon

on Friday in the week immediately preceding the week in respect

of which the application is made; or

(b) in writing so as to reach the nearest Labour Office not later than

noon on Wednesday in the week immediately preceding the week

in respect of which the application is made, and such written

application shall explain the grounds for substituting

such other day.

(2) Where the proprietor or manager of a shop who has chosen Friday or

Sunday as the day on which the shop is to remain entirely closed under subsection 3(1)

of the Act intends to alter such day to Sunday or Friday, as the case may be, the proprietor

or manager shall, not less than seven days before the alteration becomes effective—

(a) inform his employees by posting a notice in the shop; and

(b) notify the nearest Labour Office in writing of such intention.

Record of whole day holiday

5. (1) The proprietor or manager of any shop, restaurant or theatre shall keep

a record of the holidays given to each employee in Form C as specified in the Schedule

where the employee in the shop, restaurant or theatre is entitled to be given—

(a) under section 6 of the Act, a holiday of one whole day in each week;

and

(b) under subsection 7(3) of the Act, a whole holiday on five other days

in every year.

(2) The record referred to in subrule (1) shall—

(a) be kept up to date by the end of each week;

(b) be preserved for a period of at least one year after the end of the

year to which the entries in the record refer; and

(c) be kept in a conspicuous place on the premises where the

employees mentioned in the record worked or are working.

Duty of proprietor of shop where more than one business is carried on

6. (1) Where the same or different trades or businesses are carried on

separately in one shop by different proprietors, unless the exemption mentioned

in section 4 of the Act applies, the provisions of these Rules shall apply to each

such proprietor in respect of his trade or business.

(2) Where a proprietor carries on the same, or more than one, trade or

business in more than one shop, other than a shop included in a class of shops

mentioned in the Schedule to the Act, the provisions of these Rules shall apply

to such proprietor in respect of each such shop.
